title: Riddick family origins and Dr. Frank Riddick
summary: Scottish roots, Virginia ancestors, letters from Dr. Frank Riddick, and father's Mississippi land lost in the crash.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What's today's date? I was trying to mark it down on a box.
You got it on your watch so we know it's right.
Yeah, well, I'm having trouble. Yeah, the 14th.
Did you ever hear of a guy named Dave Riddick? I've only heard of one other musician named Riddick other than your family. He wasn't from here, I don't think.

Now there is a Riddick here that's a heart specialist, Dr. Frank Riddick. There are several Riddicks here. A.G. Riddick, Archie Riddick. But now, Dr. Frank Riddick, and we are definitely a distant blood relative. Because we all came from the same neck of the woods, Virginia.
Oh, I see. Yeah. Well, are you related to the Riddicks with the R-E-D? No. It's a different family.
Now, all of that, you wouldn't believe it, but we're Scotch.

And I have the history of it all, or the gene, in other words, says that it began as far back as the year 1200. And there was a different spelling of the word Rarick, and this and that and the other, and Riddick, and this. All was pronounced, though, Riddick. And it meant red dirt dairy farms. There was a barony up in North Scotland, according to the gene. Now, no proof of mind, except the gene says that. And it was pronounced Riddick. And it said that there was a recording of a tract of land in Virginia passed on into the ownership of a Riddick. There was a John Riddick. All of these names, and that there were four Riddicks that fought in the Revolution. Uh-huh. And he was the son or the grandson of one of three brothers that migrated from Virginia down into North and South Carolina into Tennessee. And Dr. Frank Riddick wrote me a letter and said that, and it read just like this, and I have it upstairs. My father said that if your father is Thomas Marshall Riddick, that we are definitely of the same clan.

And that he's told how three brothers migrated as far as Tennessee, but this one brother migrated into North Mississippi and claimed a tract of land of 5,000 acres for which my family still owned after I was born.
And the crash came and all of that. It was in Copperville, Mississippi. That was where my father was born.
Uh-huh. And this crash came when you were around 10, is that what you said? Yeah. Something like that?
